134.solution: Simplify \([\{q\wedge(\sim q\vee r)\}\wedge\{\sim p\vee(p\wedge\sim r)\}]\vee(p\wedge r)\). Now \(q\wedge(\sim q\vee r)=q\wedge r\) and \(\sim p\vee(p\wedge\sim r)=\sim p\vee\sim r\), so the bracket \(=(q\wedge r)\wedge(\sim p\vee\sim r)=q\wedge r\wedge\sim p\). The whole \(=(q\wedge r\wedge\sim p)\vee(p\wedge r)=r\wedge[(q\wedge\sim p)\vee p]=r\wedge(p\vee q)\). With \(p=S_{1},q=S_{2},r=S_{3}\): \((S_{1}\parallel S_{2})\) in series with \(S_{3}\). Among the four circuits, option B is exactly \(S_{1},S_{2}\) in parallel then \(S_{3}\) in series; option A is \((S_{1}\) series \(S_{3})\parallel S_{2}\), which is \((S_{1}\wedge S_{3})\vee S_{2}\) and is incorrect.
